He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.
新昌鄉侯 is Xinchang, not Xinxiang.

He Zeng and his colleagues firmly argued, "The central commander of the army is intelligent, divinely martial, and has talent beyond the age.
中撫軍 is Sima Yan’s office (central commander of the army), not a force named the Central Pacification Army.

That month a man of extraordinary height appeared at Xiangwu, three zhang tall, and told the county man Wang Shi, "Now there shall be great peace."
縣人王始 is one county man, Wang Shi, not “the people of the district” plus an appositive.

On yiwei he ordered the impartial evaluators (zhongzheng) of commanderies to recommend the long-neglected and obstructed according to six criteria: first, loyalty and conscientiousness sacrificing self; second, filial respect fulfilling ritual; third, harmony among brothers; fourth, purity of person with humble industry; fifth, trustworthiness and righteousness that can be relied upon; sixth, learning for one’s own moral cultivation.
郡中正 are the commandery impartial evaluators (zhongzheng), not “middle heads.”

On the day bingyin, winter, twelfth month, first year of Taishi, he set up an altar south of the suburbs; the hundred officials stood in place, together with the southern chanyu of the Xiongnu and visitors from the four barbarians numbering in the tens of thousands; he kindled the firewood offering and reported the category of his accession to the high lord, saying, "The emperor, your subject Yan, dares to use a black bull clearly to announce to the august sovereign lord: the Wei emperor has examined and aligned with the royal fortune and, clarifying heaven’s bright mandate, has used it to command Yan.
皇皇后帝 is the August Sovereign Lord; the sentence does not name heaven and earth.

A sweep of enfeoffments followed: granduncle Fu as king of Anping, a ring of royal uncles and cousins as kings of Pingyuan, Fufeng, Dongguan, Ru'yin, Liang, Langye, and more, his brother You as king of Qi, and dozens of kinsmen given kingdoms from Bohai to Dongping (footnotes [1][2] preserved in the text).

He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping; his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ruyin, Tong as king of Liang, and Lun as king of Langye; his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Lean, and Ji as king of Yan; [1] his father's elder cousin Wang as king of Yiyang; his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen; his elder cousin Hong as king of Hejian; and his younger cousin Mao as king of Dongping.

He enfeoffed his granduncle Sima Fu as king of Anping, his uncles Sima Gan as king of Pingyuan, Liang as king of Fufeng, Zhou as king of Dongguan, Jun as king of Ru'yin, Tong as king of Liang, Lun as king of Langye, his younger brother You as king of Qi, Jian as king of Le'an, Ji as king of Yan, [1] his cousin once removed Wang as king of Yiyang, his father's younger cousins Fu as king of Bohai, Huang as king of Xiapi, Gui as king of Taiyuan, Gui as king of Gaoyang, Heng as king of Changshan, Ziwen as king of Pei, [2] Tai as king of Longxi, Quan as king of Pengcheng, Sui as king of Fanyang, Sui as king of Jinan, Xun as king of Qiao, Mu as king of Zhongshan, Ling as king of Beihai, and Bin as king of Chen, his cousin Hong as king of Hejian, and his cousin Mao as king of Dongping.
皇從叔父 are father’s younger cousins, not uncles. The proposed after is right on kinship but embeds Chinese graphs; the paired Gui and Sui are distinguished by Taiyuan/Gaoyang and Fanyang/Jinan.

The chief generals and ministers received ducal fiefs—Shi Bao grand marshal of Leling, Chen Qian of Gaoping, Jia Chong elevated to chariots-and-cavalry general and duke of Lu, Pei Xiu duke of Julu, and so through the senior statesmen.

He appointed Shi Bao, general of swift cavalry, grand marshal and duke of Leling; Chen Qian duke of Gaoping; Jia Chong general of chariots and cavalry and duke of Lu; Pei Xiu duke of Julu; Xun Xu duke of Jibei; Zheng Chong grand tutor and duke of Shouguang; Wang Xiang grand guardian and duke of Suiling; He Zeng grand commandant and duke of Langling; Wang Chen general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling; Xun Yi duke of Linhuai; and Wei Guan duke of Ziyang.
The sentence names eleven men with offices and fiefs; the original English stopped after Pei Xiu.
Summer, fifth month, wuchen: “The Chenliu king, Cao Shang, still files humble memorials on trifles—that is no way to honor him.
Summer, fifth month, wuchen: “The Chenliu king still conducts himself with modesty and files a memorial on every trifle—that is no way to honor him.
操尚謙沖 describes the Chenliu king’s modest conduct; Cao Shang is not a name.
In summer, fifth month, on wuchen the edict said, "The king of Chenliu, Cao Shang, is still modest; on every matter he submits a memorial—this is not the way to show him special honor.
In summer, fifth month, on wuchen the edict said, "The king of Chenliu still conducts himself with modesty and submits a memorial on every matter—this is not the way to show him special honor.
操尚 is “still conducts himself,” not the personal name Cao Shang.
On renzi [5] Wang Shen—swift-cavalry general and duke of Boling—passed away.
On renzi [5] Wang Chen—swift-cavalry general and duke of Boling—passed away.
王沈 is Wang Chen (沈 as chén), the Boling duke already named above, not Wang Shen.
On the day renzi [5], Wang Shen, general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling, died.
On the day renzi [5], Wang Chen, general of swift cavalry and duke of Boling, died.
王沈 is Wang Chen, not Wang Shen.
On yiwei in the ninth month Huangfu Tao and Fu Xun, as remonstrators, sent up blunt advice; the clerks moved to bury their petitions.
On yiwei in the ninth month Huangfu Tao and Fu Xuan, as remonstrators, sent up blunt advice; the clerks moved to bury their petitions.
傅玄 is Fu Xuan; Fu Xun is a different name.
That December the old “agriculture” jurisdictions were converted into ordinary counties.
In the twelfth month the old “agriculture” jurisdictions were converted into ordinary counties.
十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not Gregorian December.

On wuzi he mused: “When the ancients set up symbolic punishments, the multitude did not offend; today we slaughter whole clans yet treason persists—what has become of moral government?
古設象刑 names the ancients and symbolic punishments; Yao and Shun are not in the sentence.
Second month, gengzi: the Chenliu ex-emperor’s apanage gained a full household staff—chancellor, household director, tomb wardens, artisans, cooks, and a band with carriages.
Second month, gengzi: the Shanyang duke’s state gained a full household staff—chancellor, household director, tomb wardens, artisans, cooks, and a band with carriages.
山陽公國 is the duke of Shanyang’s state, not the Chenliu ex-emperor’s apanage.
December: Kong Zhen, “continuer of the sage,” was moved to the smaller fief of “village that honors the sage.”
In the twelfth month: Kong Zhen, “continuer of the sage,” was moved to the smaller fief of “village that honors the sage.”
十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

The twelfth month brought the five-point provincial charter—self-cultivation, care for the people, relief for the helpless, agriculture over commerce, and an end to clientage.
十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

In the second month he carved out Qin province, combining the five Longyou commanderies under Yong with Jincheng from the Hexi frontier and Yinping from the Hanzhong basin.
二月 is the lunar second month, not February.

On jiwei, Zhuge Liang's grandson Zhuge Jing was assigned an office suited to his talents.
諸葛亮孫京 is Zhuge Liang’s grandson Jing; 孫 is kinship, not the surname Sun.

On jiwei, an edict ordered that Zhuge Jing, grandson of Zhuge Liang, chancellor of Shu, be appointed to office according to his abilities.
孫京 means grandson Jing of the Zhuge house, not a man named Sun Jing.
December: every province was told to nominate bold and exceptional warriors.
In the twelfth month: every province was told to nominate bold and exceptional warriors.

In the twelfth month: Sun Xiu, Wu’s Xiakou commander, defected with his army and received a ducal title and swift-cavalry command.
十二月 is the lunar twelfth month, not December.

In the eleventh month, on the dingsi day, Ji Shu, duke of Wei, died.

In the sixth month: Yi’s gate captain Zhang Hong murdered inspector Huangfu Yan on a false charge of treason.

In the twelfth month: Yang Zhao failed against Lu Kang and pulled back.

Ninth year, spring, first month, xinyou: Zheng Mao, minister of works and marquis of Miling, died.

Second month, guisi: Shi Bao, steward of the masters of the people and duke of Leling, died.

Eighth month: Liang tribes raided Jincheng until Sima Jun, king of Ru'yin, cut down chiefs such as Qi Wenni.

Wu generals Sun Zun and Li Cheng led a host to raid Jiangxia; prefect Ji Xi defeated them.

陝南山 is the range south of Shan/Shaan, not Shanxi province.

The second month brought relief for families swamped with daughters: any household raising five girls was excused from labor levies, so married soldiers could still serve without ruining their kin.

Earlier, Dunhuang had fallen into chaos after Yin Qu’s death: Linghu Feng ousted Liang Cheng, the magistrate who was acting as prefect, and seized the prefecture.
燉煌令梁澄領太守事: Liang Cheng was the county magistrate acting as prefect, not an “acting magistrate.” The proposed sentence needs a comma before “and seized.”

Jiaxu [15]: a comet shone in the asterism Di.
孛于氐 is a comet in the lodge Di, not a reference to the Di people.

In the eleventh month: twin white dragons in Liang.
十一月 is the lunar eleventh month, not November.

In the twelfth month he called scholar Huangfu Mi to tutor the heir and made empress Yang’s father Yang Jun marquis of Linjin.

In the sixth month: flash floods in Yi and Liang drowned three hundred and swamped auxiliary granaries.

He established the imperial son Wei as king of Shiping, Yun as king of Puyang, Gai as king of Xindu, Xia as king of Qinghe, and marquis Yang Hu of Juping as marquis of Nancheng.

Dingwei: He Zeng, grand preceptor and duke of Langling, died.

Gengshen: Xiling fell; Liu Xian, Cheng Qu, and Zheng Guang died defending it [25].

On the day gengshen they also took Xiling, killing Xiling commander and general who guards the army Liu Xian [25], general who campaigns south Cheng Qu, and Xiling intendant Zheng Guang.

孫氏大將戰亡之家 are families of Sun generals killed in battle; 復十年 remits labor service, not a generic tax holiday.
Bingyin [29]: Sun Hao was paraded before the court amid cheers.

Dingmao: Linglu wine was poured for the ancestors.

On the day dingmao fine wine from Linglu was offered in the grand temple.

Each man receives a named office or fief, and 增封 is increased enfeoffment, not added revenue.
Sima Mu regained kingship as ruler of Gaoyang.
Sima Mu, marquis of Danshui, was enfeoffed as king of Gaoyang.
封丹水侯睦爲高陽王 is a new kingship from the Danshui marquisate; the text does not say he regained a kingdom.

Seventh month: steppe raider Kecheni hit Xiping and Haomen, killing three hundred officers.

In autumn, the seventh month, the tribesman Kecheni raided Xiping and Haomen, killing more than three hundred commanders and captains downward.

Cheshi’s forward king sent his heir to Luoyang.
In the eighth month the forward division of Cheshi sent a son to serve at court.

Jiwei: Prince Yanzuo became king of Leping.
Jiwei: the imperial younger brother Yanzuo was enfeoffed as king of Leping.

Wuchen: Sima Zan of Guanghan died.
Twelfth month, wuchen: Sima Zan, king of Guanghan, died.
The death is dated 十二月戊辰.
Taikang 2, spring: Huainan and Danyang shook.
Taikang 2, spring, second month: Huainan and Danyang suffered earthquakes.
二年春二月 names the second month; 地震 are earthquakes.
Summer: five more Yi peoples asked for enrollment.
Summer, sixth month: five states of the eastern Yi submitted.
夏六月 dates the event; 東夷五國 are five states, and 內附 is submission.
Floods on the Yangzi and at Taishan displaced three hundred families.
Floods at Jiangxia and Mount Tai swept away more than three hundred households.
江夏 is Jiangxia, not the Yangzi, and 三百餘家 is more than three hundred households.
August: a comet crossed the Zhang mansion.
Eighth month: a broom star appeared in the Zhang lunar lodge.
八月 is the lunar eighth month; 星孛于張 is a broom star in the Zhang lodge.

Winter, tenth month: Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Changli.
Jiawu: Zhang Hua took command on the Youzhou frontier.
Jiawu: Zhang Hua, a master of writing, was appointed commander of all military affairs in You province.

Intercalary bingzi: Li Yin, steward of the masters of the people, died.
Intercalary bingzi: Li Yin, Minister over the Masses and marquis of Guanglu, died.
司徒 is Minister over the Masses, and 廣陸侯 is in the death notice; the proposal dropped the marquisate.
In the intercalary month, on the day bingzi, Li Yin, steward of the masters of the people and marquis of Guanglu, died.
In the intercalary month, on the day bingzi, Li Yin, minister over the masses and marquis of Guanglu, died.
司徒 is the minister over the masses; “steward of the masters of the people” is a misleading calque.

Former Wu generals Guan Gong and Bo Feng raised troops in revolt, killed the magistrate of Jianye, then besieged Yang province; Ji Xi, inspector of Xu province, campaigned and pacified them.

Taikang 4, jiashen [33]: Wei Shu and Sima Huang took the left and right vice-presidencies.
Taikang 4, spring, first month, jiashen [33]: Wei Shu moved from right vice-president of the secretariat to left vice-president, and Sima Huang, king of Xiapi, became right vice-president.

Jichou: Shi was promoted from Changle village marquis to king of Beihai.
Jichou of the second month: Shi, marquis of Changle village, was established as king of Beihai.
二月己丑 dates the enfeoffment; 立 is “established.”
Summer: Sima Ling of Rencheng died.
Summer, fourth month: Sima Ling, king of Rencheng, died.
夏四月 dates the death, and 任城王 is a kingship.
Jihai: Sima Zhou, king of Langye, died.
Jihai of the fifth month: Sima Zhou, great general and king of Langye, died.
五月己亥 dates the death, and he is 大將軍 as well as 琅邪王.
The Liaodong princedom was downgraded to Donglai for Sima Rui.
Sima Rui was transferred from king of Liaodong to king of Donglai.

June: salaries for the nine chamberlains were raised.
Sixth month: the ritual stipends of the nine ministers were increased.
六月 is the lunar sixth month, and 禮秩 is ritual rank and stipend, not salary alone.
Renzi: Sima Huang took Qing military command.
Renzi of the seventh month: Sima Huang, king of Xiapi and right vice-president, was made commander of all military affairs in Qing province.
秋七月壬子 dates the appointment; he is 尚書右僕射 and 下邳王 made 都督青州諸軍事.
Shanshan sent a royal hostage and received the “return to righteousness” marquis title.
Eighth month: Shanshan sent a son to serve at court, and he was provisionally made marquis who returns to righteousness.
八月 dates the mission; 遣子入侍 and 假其歸義侯 give the son a provisional marquisate.
Wuwu: Sima Gai of Xindu died.
Wuwu of the eleventh month: Sima Gai, king of Xindu, died.
冬十一月戊午 dates the death.

Wei Shu became minister over the masses.

Wei Shu of the masters of writing was appointed minister over the masses.
司徒 is minister over the masses, not a household steward.
Gengwu of the twelfth month: a grand review was held at the Xuanwu stand.
十二月庚午 dates the review; 大閱 is a grand review, and “another” is not in the Chinese.
Bingwu: a roof-beam snapped in Gaozu’s temple.
Bingwu: a roof-beam snapped in Emperor Xuan's temple.
宣帝廟 is Emperor Xuan’s temple, not Gaozu’s.
Bingyin: Prince Dian of the southern palace became king of Changle.
Bingyin of the second month: Dian, son of the king of Nangong, was established as king of Changle.

June: the “Yellow Sand” review prison was created.
Sixth month: the “Yellow Sand” review prison was created.
六月 is the lunar sixth month, not June.
Seventh month, wushen: Prince Hui died.
Seventh month, wushen: the imperial son Hui died.
皇子恢 is an imperial son; “Prince Hui” drops 皇子.
September brought gales, floods in five provinces, and black frost.
The ninth month brought gales, floods in five provinces, and black frost.
九月 is the lunar ninth month, not September.
Jiachen: Sima Fu of Taiyuan died.
Jiachen of the eleventh month: Sima Fu, king of Taiyuan, died.

Gengwu of the twelfth month: a great amnesty.
十二月庚午 dates the amnesty.
Intercalary month: Du Yu, great general who guards the south and marquis of Dangyang, died.
鎮南大將軍 and 當陽侯 belong to the death notice.
March frost hurt mulberries and wheat in six jurisdictions.
The third month frost hurt mulberries and wheat in six jurisdictions.
三月 is the lunar third month, not March.
Bingzi: Liu Kang, last Han-title noble, died.
Bingzi of the ninth month: Liu Kang, duke of Shanyang, died.
山陽公劉康 is the duke of Shanyang, dated 九月丙子; “last Han-title noble” is a gloss.
Winter: landslides and flash floods in Nan’an.
Winter, tenth month: landslides and flash floods in Nan’an.
Jiashen: a ten-day army review at Xuanwu.
Jiashen of the twelfth month: a grand review at the Xuanwu stand lasted ten days.
十二月甲申 dates the review.
Summer, fifth month: thirteen commanderies and principalities had drought.
夏五月 dates the drought, and 郡國十三 are commanderies and principalities, not provinces.

August: eleven Yi peoples asked to join Jin.
Eighth month: eleven Yi peoples asked to join Jin.

Wuyin: Sima Jun of Fufeng died.
Wuyin of the ninth month: Sima Jun, general of the agile cavalry and king of Fufeng, died.
九月戊寅 dates the death, and he is 驃騎將軍 as well as 扶風王.
Censors toured flood-hit counties with relief mandates.
Twelfth month: investigating censors were sent to tour commanderies that had suffered flood.
十二月 dates the tour; 侍御史 inspect flood-hit 郡, and the text does not mention relief mandates.

歸于家 is sent home; the text does not say they were freed to marry.
September: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.
Ninth month: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.
九月 is the lunar ninth month, not September.
Winter: Li Feng’s mutiny in southern Jiangxi.

Fifth month: Sima Qi of Yiyang lost his kingship for crime, becoming village marquis of Sanzongting.

Taikang 10, summer, fourth month: Liu Xiao, prefect of Jingzhao, and Liang Liu, prefect of Yangping, were each granted a thousand hu of grain for their administration.
十年夏四月 dates the grants; Liu Xiao is 京兆太守 and Liang Liu 陽平太守.

Fifth month: Murong Hui yielded while eleven Yi realms joined Jin.
五月 is the lunar fifth month, not May.

Gengzi of the sixth month: Liu Jin, duke of Shanyang, died.
六月庚子 dates the death; 山陽公 is duke of Shanyang, not “mountain-yang duke.”

戊午 is marked with a note after the seventh-month entry; Hou Shiguang's tour is kept in Taishi 4 without a day conversion.

The frost sentence is marked with note 19. No day conversion is made.
The submission list is marked with note 20. It is kept as the year Xianning 3 without further dating.
The hail notice is marked with note 22. No day conversion is made.
The tomb-opening is marked with note 23. It is kept in Xianning 5 without a day.
The campaign sentence is marked with note 24. The launch stays an eleventh-month event of Xianning 5, western years 279-280, with no day.
Liu Xian's death is marked with note 25. The Xiling deaths stay in Taikang 1 without a day conversion.
Stone City is marked with note 27. Sun Hao's surrender stays in the third month of Taikang 1 without a day conversion.
乙酉 is marked with note 28 and is not securely inside the third month. The amnesty and era change stay in Taikang 1 (280) without a day conversion.
Note 29 is on bingyin. No day is converted.
Wuchen of the twelfth month of Taikang 1 is dated 281 from the standard table (that month begins 8 January 281). External, marked uncertain.
Note 30 stands alone. No person and no date.
Note 31 is on the Ping and Ning inspectors' triennial report. The English that abolishes Pingzhou is repaired.
Note 32 sits inside the appointment list. The twelfth month of Taikang 3 begins 16 January 283, so these appointments are dated 283, uncertain, from the standard table.
Note 33 is on jiashen of Taikang 4. A first month beginning on xinchou (14 February 283) cannot contain jiashen. The year is kept as 283 and the day is not converted.
Wuwu has no month of its own. It stays in Taikang 4 (283) without a day conversion.
The text says the third month of Taikang 4 began on xinchou. The standard table gives gengzi for that new moon. The year is kept as 283 and the day is not converted.
The twelfth month of Taikang 4 begins 5 January 284. Gengwu is dated 284, uncertain, from the standard table.
Gaozu in the idiomatic English is repaired to Emperor Xuan. His life is bounded only as before 284, from the temple already standing.
The beam broke in Emperor Xuan's temple. His life is not dated from 284.
Gengwu of the twelfth month of Taikang 5 falls on 3 January 285. Dated 285, uncertain.
The embassies sit between the twelfth month and the intercalary month, so the western year may be 284 or 285. No envoy is named.
The intercalary month is the intercalary twelfth of Taikang 5, beginning 23 January 285. Du Yu's death is dated 285, uncertain.
Note 36 is on the jiashen new moon. The standard table gives gengshen for the first of Taikang 6. The year is kept as 285 and the day is not converted.
One character 子 covers the sons of both Qiuci and Yanqi, so neither son is given that span as an exclusive surface.
The twelfth month of Taikang 6 begins on jiashen, 12 January 286. The review and Wang Jun's death on gengzi are dated 286, uncertain.
The twelfth month of Taikang 7 begins 2 January 287. The censors, the palace women, the mourning decree, and the jihai red snow follow that month and are dated 287, uncertain.
The eleventh month of Taikang 8 begins 22 December 287 and continues into January 288. Xiao Fu is dated 287-288, uncertain.
The twelfth month of Taikang 8 begins 21 January 288. Jiang Di's execution is dated 288, uncertain.
The twelfth month of Taikang 9 begins 9 January 289. Ying's enfeoffment is dated 289, uncertain. 英 is not 穎.
Bingchen cannot fall inside a Taikang 10 eleventh month that the standard table starts on renxu. The year is kept as 289 and the day is not converted.
皇孫 entails an unnamed father between Sima Yan and Yu. He is recorded without a surface.
Di is taken as Yun's son and Yi (儀) as Wei's son because the previous sentence identifies the kings of Puyang and Shiping. Marked strongly inferred.
弟 is written once, before Dan. You, Cui, and Juan are taken as further younger brothers of Jin from the parallel list. That extension is strongly inferred.
Note 39. Gengyin does not fall in a twelfth month that the standard table starts on xinmao (29 Dec 289). Dated only as Taikang 10's twelfth month, 289-290, uncertain.
Death in Taixi 1, fourth month, aged 55 sui. Taixi 1 = 290 is the standard conversion, external. The day is not given a Gregorian date.
Xu Yun's death and Emperor Wen's reign have no year in this chunk. Bounded only as before 290.
元海 is rendered Liu Yuan. The surname Liu is not in the Chinese.
The collation identifies Prince of Pei but gives no life year. Li the collator is also undated.
The note says this month's stem-branch sequence is inconsistent.
The note says the fifth-month range is impossible as given.
Ding Guojun is cited with no year. The sixth-month new moon is a textual variant, jiashen versus bingshen.
Wan Yu's life year is not in the note. Only the graph is compared.
Wen Shu, Wen Chu, and Wen Yang are treated as one man because Pei Songzhi says so. King Yao is 繇, not a man named Yao.
Taishi 5 = 269 and Taikang 3 = 282 are the standard conversions of era years the note itself names.
Wu Yan's beheading is not given a year in this note, so the death has no western year.
The fifteenth day equaling renyin is a calendar argument. No western year is stated.
Taishi 5 = 269 and Taikang 4 = 283 are external conversions of era years named in the Kaoyi quotation. Murong Hui's birth and Shegui's death use those years, marked inferred.
The note shows that jiashen cannot be the new moon if the first month begins on xinchou. No person, and the day is not given a western date.
If the third month begins on gengzi, xinchou is day 2. The note itself doubts the new-moon graph. No western day is invented.
Dian, the Prince of Nangong, and Fu are undated. You is the variant graph 祐 for Dian, not Sima You.
Jiashen cannot be the new moon if the month begins on gengshen. No western day is invented.
Taikang 9 = 288 is the standard conversion of the era year the biography names. No reignId. Used for Wei's departure, Ying's enfeoffment, and as context for Hun's being made heir.

Xianhe 6 = 331 is the standard conversion of 咸和六年. It dates Zhen's enfeoffment only. Hun is named there as Zhen's father and as king of Zhangwu, but that later annal is not used as Hun's active year. Ying may be a miswriting of Hun.
Gengyin cannot fall in a twelfth month that begins on xinmao. The treatises put it on the twenty-ninth of the eleventh month. No western day is invented.
Sun Pingzi is undated. The memorial is about the month of the portent, not about his own life.
